title: Egress-window capacity guard for VPC health and latency SLOs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an 'egress-window capacity guard' for Private (VPC) deployments: a lightweight, deployable telemetry + IaC pattern that combines throughput watermarking, moving-window token accounting, and tail-latency fencing to prevent cascading latency and saturation during upgrades and traffic spikes. The goal is to provide deterministic SLO enforcement (latency, error rate, token throughput) using small-footprint probes and Terraform module hooks so customers can get safe autoscaling and graceful degradation without increasing operator burden.
slo_definitions: Latency: streaming token p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms during normal load
Saturation: node-level token queue depth should not exceed 85% capacity for >30s
Throughput watermark: sustained token throughput above configured baseline should trigger autoscale or shed policies
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module adds egress-window metric exporter and config hooks (no manual agent install required)
Operator console shows per-VPC watermark, token ledger, and a 'fenced' state when tail latency policies are violated
Canary rollout demonstrates graceful degradation: low-priority requests shed, high-priority continue with fallback model variant
Integration tests for upgrade path: rolling restart with simulated token-exhaustion does not exceed error-rate SLO
Runbook and alerting thresholds documented in the private deployment runbook (Confluence link added)
implementation_notes: Design: moving-window token ledger implemented as lightweight sidecar with local in-memory ring buffer + periodic aggregated export (Prometheus) to avoid frequent control-plane calls
Decision: prefer watermark extrapolation over instantaneous token counters to reduce noise and false positives
Trade-off: sidecar increases per-node footprint but allows local decision and near-zero control-plane latency for shedding
Compatibility: sidecar supports IPv4-only and VPC endpoint configurations; will surface flags in Terraform module (module v1.3)
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike complete — prototyped moving-window ledger in Go, local ring buffer + Prom client. Observed low CPU overhead (~1-2%) under benchmark.

2026-03-05: Integration test harness updated to simulate token floods and tail-latency events. Early canary showed expected 'fenced' transition and shed behavior. Test run: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/egress-window-canary/57

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives causing unnecessary shedding during short spikes — Mitigation: use hysteresis and multi-window confirmation (30s and 5m windows)
Risk: sidecar memory leak under extreme churn — Mitigation: add memory limits and sentinel eviction, plus e2e stress test
Risk: Terraform module misconfiguration in customer IaC — Mitigation: sensible defaults, thorough docs, and a preflight check command in the module
review_feedback: PM (Alexei Volkov): prefer conservative defaults and explicit opt-in for legacy customers
Design (Sasha Patel): request for clearer Console visuals for 'fenced' state and per-route breakdown
Security (Leena Gupta): require KMS-backed exporter credentials and audit log entries for fence-trigger events
SRE (Priya Nair): add synthetic probes that mimic RL scenario for continuous validation
